# US-4127 — Update order status from the order detail page

## Summary

Adds a `PATCH /orders/{id}/status` endpoint that allows support agents to update an order's status directly. The endpoint is restricted to users with the `Support` role and records the time of each status change in the new `StatusUpdatedAt` column.

## Changes

- **New endpoint** `PATCH /orders/{id:int}/status` in `OrdersController`, authorized to the `Support` role only.
  - Returns `204 NoContent` on success.
  - Returns `404 NotFound` when the order does not exist.
- **New DTO** `UpdateOrderStatusRequest` with validation restricting `Status` to `Pending`, `Shipped`, `Delivered`, or `Cancelled`.
- **New service method** `OrderService.UpdateStatusAsync` updates the order status and sets `StatusUpdatedAt` to `DateTime.UtcNow`.
- **Database migration** `20261101_add_status_updated_at.sql` adds the nullable `StatusUpdatedAt` column to the `Orders` table.
- **Unit test** `UpdateStatus_ReturnsNoContent_WhenOrderExists` added to `OrdersControllerTests`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] An agent with the Support role can change an order's status to Shipped from the order detail page.
- [x] The change records the timestamp of the status update.
- [x] The endpoint rejects requests from users without the Support role.

---

PR description to grade:

```markdown
## What
Fixes `BUG-3388` — checkout was throwing a 500 when an order had no discount record, causing ~2.1% of checkouts (≈180 orders) to fail last week.

## Root cause
`OrderService.GetTotal` accessed `order.Discount.Percentage` directly, which threw a `NullReferenceException` when `Discount` was null.

## Changes

# TECH-91 — Extract pricing rules out of OrderService

## Summary

Moves all order pricing logic out of `OrderService` into a new dedicated `PriceCalculator` class. `OrderService` now delegates to `PriceCalculator` for subtotals, discounts, and totals.

## Why

`OrderService` has grown to ~1,400 lines and every pricing change requires touching order orchestration code. Extracting the calculation rules lets the pricing team iterate independently and reduces review scope for pricing-only changes.

## Changes

- **Added `src/Application/Orders/PriceCalculator.cs`**
  - `Subtotal(Order)` — sum of `UnitPrice * Quantity` across order lines
  - `DiscountAmount(Order)` — percentage-based discount from the subtotal
  - `Total(Order)` — subtotal minus discount
- **Updated `src/Application/Orders/OrderService.cs`**
  - `OrderService` now holds a private `PriceCalculator` instance
  - `GetTotal` delegates to `_pricing.Total(order)` instead of computing inline
- **Updated `tests/Orders/OrderServiceTests.cs`**
  - Added `GetTotal_MatchesPriceCalculator_ForDiscountedOrder` to verify `OrderService.GetTotal` and `PriceCalculator.Total` return the same value for a discounted order

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Pricing rules live in a dedicated `PriceCalculator` class.
- [x] `OrderService` delegates to that class.
- [x] No behaviour changes; existing tests continue to pass.

## How to test

```bash
dotnet test
```

> There are no functional changes; the new test acts as a parity check between `OrderService` and `PriceCalculator`.
```
